source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, check Chassis information and detail information.
source_snapshot.criteria: Data should be readable and correct.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES assumes `/redfish/v1/Chassis/FRU_SYS/Sensors`, selects only `.Temperatures`, disables TLS verification and uses fragile jq string/numeric composition; it omits collection pagination, non-temperature sensors, units, state, thresholds, identity and freshness.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly requires a complete vendor-mapped unit/threshold/freshness-aware sensor matrix and no-stimulus boundary, but leaves those finite Project inputs as an engineering-decision gate.

old_problem: A readable temperature list is not a complete or correctness-preserving Miramar sensor test. The assumed path may not exist, the source covers WebUI chassis detail rather than temperature-only API output, and values without durable sensor identity, units, status, thresholds and timestamps can be stale or mis-scaled. The prior review found these gaps but retained Pending for Project sensor semantics.
disposition_reason: Resolve the Project-defined Miramar sensor population and actual supported Redfish/OEM collections, enumerate every member and page, preserve actual rendered WebUI evidence, and validate per-sensor identity, type, reading, units, status, threshold configuration and freshness against the approved sensor specification. Missing thresholds prevent PASS but are NOT READY inputs, not a new engineering decision; no sensor stimulus or configuration change is allowed.
decision_basis: XLSX row 964, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 965 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 965 / variant 1a42895db64c9648.

The source does not require IPMI FRU comparison for Miramar_Sensor. Importing the preceding FRU method would invent coverage; actual WebUI chassis/detail remains the primary source surface and structured telemetry is supporting evidence.

DMTF Sensor resources distinguish Reading, ReadingUnits, ReadingType, Status, PhysicalContext, related items and threshold objects. Numeric value without those fields cannot establish meaning or correctness.

Temperature-only selection reduces coverage unless the approved Miramar map proves every applicable sensor is temperature. Voltage, current, power, fan/rotational, discrete/count or OEM types must be handled when present in the Project population.

ED-08, ED-14, ED-15, ED-16, ED-17, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 require actual visual evidence, approved thresholds and safe no-injection handling; ED-33 through ED-38 allow the sensor map/limits to be Project readiness inputs without guessed OEM paths.

test_case.test_name: Validate the complete Miramar sensor population, units, thresholds, health and freshness
test_case.purpose: Verify every Project-applicable Miramar sensor is uniquely present and readable in the actual BMC WebUI and approved structured telemetry, with correct physical identity, reading type/unit, value, availability/health, configured thresholds and freshness under the approved operating context, without changing thresholds or stimulating hardware.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/platform/firmware/WebUI identity and approved definition of Miramar hardware scope/topology
Authoritative complete Miramar sensor manifest with durable sensor ID, UI label, physical context/related component, expected present/unsupported/disabled status and sensor type
Service-root-discovered Redfish Sensor collection(s), legacy Thermal/Power mapping or explicitly approved OEM telemetry resources with schema versions and pagination behavior
Per-sensor expected ReadingUnits/ReadingType, precision/resolution/tolerance, valid operating range and configured threshold matrix; no PASS threshold may be invented
Approved Status/availability, zero/null/NaN/absent/disabled/unsupported and data-age/cache/freshness semantics for the current operating context
Actual WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs Miramar table/detail mapping, visual capture method, trusted TLS/protected credentials and evidence/redaction storage
test_case.test_command: READ ONLY. Verify immutable target and approved Miramar topology. Discover the actual supported Sensor collection(s), legacy Thermal/Power resources or approved OEM telemetry links from the service; traverse all pagination and every member instead of assuming `/FRU_SYS/Sensors`. Preserve complete structured responses and timestamps without concatenating numeric readings into strings. For each expected sensor, bind durable Id/MemberId/Name to the approved physical context/related component and record ReadingType, numeric or discrete Reading, ReadingUnits, Status.State/Health, thresholds, min/max range, precision/accuracy fields when supported and source/data age. Keep zero, null, NaN, absent, disabled, unavailable, unsupported, unauthorized and transport failure distinct. Open the actual rendered BMC WebUI Inventory and LEDs Miramar table and each required detail, capture visual evidence, and reconcile membership, labels, units, values, status and thresholds within the approved simultaneous-sampling/freshness tolerance. Compare readings and configured thresholds only to approved Project limits. Repeat read-only sampling only as specified; do not clear logs, change thresholds, inject faults, alter loads/fans/power, reset or reboot.
test_case.expected_result: Every expected applicable Miramar sensor appears exactly once with the approved physical association, type and unit; every approved absent/disabled/unsupported member uses its documented representation. Structured and actual WebUI values/status/thresholds reconcile within approved precision and freshness tolerance, all configured thresholds exactly match the Project sensor specification, and current readings/status meet the approved operating-context acceptance limits. No missing, duplicate, stale, unparseable, unitless-without-policy or unexpected sensor exists and no configuration or hardware state changes.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete collection/page traversal, exact membership and physical mapping, actual rendered WebUI evidence, correct type/unit, fresh readable value/status and exact approved threshold configuration for every applicable sensor. A temperature-only list, readable number, Healthy label or guessed path cannot pass. Missing/duplicate sensor, unknown unit, stale/unavailable reading outside policy, UI/API mismatch, unapproved threshold, out-of-limit value or unclassified absence is FAIL. If the Project sensor manifest, limit/threshold matrix or freshness policy is missing, execution is NOT READY and no PASS may be issued; no threshold is invented to resolve Pending.
safety_gate: Use certificate-verified protected GET/read operations discovered from the service; do not use `curl -k`, expose credentials or assume a nested Sensors URI.
Keep the case strictly observational. Prohibit threshold/setpoint changes, sensor enable/disable, fault/error injection, workload/load manipulation, fan control, reset, reboot and all power actions.
Enumerate the complete approved sensor population and pagination; do not infer non-temperature sensors from a temperature sample or collapse duplicate labels without durable identity.
Preserve numbers as typed values with explicit units and timestamps; do not coerce to fragile strings or treat zero as absent/unavailable.
Apply only approved per-sensor thresholds, precision and freshness. Without them report NOT READY, never PASS based on readability or generic ranges.
Retain actual rendered WebUI evidence and raw structured artifacts; stop on mapping, unit, freshness or authority ambiguity without automatic stimulus or retry.
expected_evidence: Immutable target/schema/WebUI identity, approved Miramar topology and complete expected sensor manifest
Complete paginated raw structured telemetry with member links, timestamps, certificate result and protected artifact hashes
Per-sensor matrix of durable ID, UI label, physical context, type, typed reading, units, state/health, thresholds, precision/range and freshness
Actual rendered WebUI Miramar table/detail visual artifacts and simultaneous API/UI reconciliation results
Approved per-sensor limit/threshold/absence/freshness specification and explicit membership/threshold/current-reading outcomes
Preserved SEL/audit evidence, no-threshold-change/no-stimulus/no-reset/no-power proof and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is intended. On ambiguous sensor identity, unknown unit, stale/unparseable reading, threshold mismatch or UI/API disagreement, stop, preserve/redact evidence and obtain the authoritative sensor map/limits. Do not change thresholds, stimulate hardware, clear logs, reset, reboot, power-cycle or automatically retry a failed DUT operation.

source_conflict.reason: The Master broadly requires Miramar sensor data to be readable/correct in the actual WebUI. DeepSeek's temperature-only API path is incomplete implementation guidance, not a conflicting source purpose.

blocked.reason: Complete read-only sensor validation is technically defined. The exact Miramar population, limits, thresholds and freshness are finite Project prerequisites.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Miramar topology/sensor manifest; actual standard/OEM collection paths; per-sensor type/unit/limits/thresholds; absence/status/freshness rules; WebUI mapping; trust and evidence storage.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; READ-ONLY MIRAMAR SENSOR REVIEW ONLY; NO API, WEBUI, THRESHOLD, STIMULUS, POWER OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

project_authority: The Project/vendor sensor specification defines Miramar membership, topology, units, limits, configured thresholds, acceptable state and freshness. These parameters enable a deterministic read-only comparison; their absence prevents PASS but does not require a new engineering decision.
